sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: If you grew up speaking a language other than English,
sentences.zh: 如果你从小说的不是英语，

sentences.en: you probably reach for words in your native tongue without even thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 你可能在不经意间就会脱口而出母语中的词汇。

sentences.en: There are phrases in every language that are deeply evocative and often untranslatable.
sentences.zh: 每种语言中都有一些含义深远且往往难以翻译的短语。

sentences.en: If you're studying a new language, you might discover these phrases not in your textbooks,
sentences.zh: 如果你正在学习一门新语言，你可能会发现这些短语并不在教科书里，

sentences.en: but when you're hanging out with friends.
sentences.zh: 而是在你和朋友闲聊时学到的。

sentences.en: My name is Jennifer Giacone Cruz.
sentences.zh: 我叫詹妮弗·贾科内·克鲁兹。

sentences.en: Jennifer moved to Japan for graduate school.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗搬到日本读研究生。

sentences.en: And I ended up living there for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 最终我在那里住了10年。

sentences.en: It took just one week of living in Japan for Jennifer to pick up an important new term.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗在日本生活仅一周，就学会了一个重要的新词。

sentences.en: Here's what she says it means.
sentences.zh: 以下是她对这个词含义的解释。

sentences.en: It's this phrase that describes something between I can't be bothered,
sentences.zh: 这个短语描述了一种介于“我懒得动”，

sentences.en: or I don't want to do it,
sentences.zh: 或者“我不想做”，

sentences.en: or I recognize the incredible effort that goes into something,
sentences.zh: 或者“我意识到做某事需要付出巨大的努力”，

sentences.en: even though it shouldn't be so much of an effort.
sentences.zh: 尽管它本不该需要那么多努力的感觉。

sentences.en: Still don't have a clear picture?
sentences.zh: 还是没听明白？

sentences.en: Imagine this.
sentences.zh: 想象一下这个场景。

sentences.en: It's a Sunday afternoon and it's raining outside and you're at home in your pajamas,
sentences.zh: 一个周日的下午，外面下着雨，你穿着睡衣待在家里，

sentences.en: all nice and cuddly, maybe watching Netflix or something.
sentences.zh: 感觉既舒适又惬意，可能正在看网飞之类的节目。

sentences.en: And you suddenly get a craving for potato chips and you realize that you have none in the kitchen
sentences.zh: 突然你想吃薯片了，却发现厨房里什么都没有，

sentences.en: and there's nothing else you really want to eat.
sentences.zh: 而且也没有其他真正想吃的东西。

sentences.en: And maybe the convenience store, the shop is really not that far away.
sentences.zh: 也许便利店离得并不远。

sentences.en: Maybe it's even less than 100 meters away, but you just can't bring yourself to even throw your coat on over your pajamas
sentences.zh: 可能还不到100米，但你就是无法让自己穿上外套套在睡衣外面，

sentences.en: and put your boots on and go outside and walk those 100 meters because somehow it would break the coziness.
sentences.zh: 穿上靴子出门走那100米，因为那样会破坏这种舒适感。

sentences.en: And it's just too much of an effort and you can't be bothered to do it, even though it's such a small thing.
sentences.zh: 这实在太费劲了，你懒得去做，尽管这只是件小事。

sentences.en: So it's mendok sai.
sentences.zh: 这就是“mendok sai”（麻烦）。

sentences.en: The moment she heard it, Jennifer realized mendok sai was incredibly useful.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗听到这个词的瞬间，就意识到“mendok sai”非常有用。

sentences.en: It describes this feeling so perfectly in such a wonderfully packaged, encapsulated way.
sentences.zh: 它以一种极其精妙、高度浓缩的方式完美地描述了这种感觉。

sentences.en: And you can just, it rolls off the tongue and you can just throw it out.
sentences.zh: 而且它朗朗上口，你可以随口说出来。

sentences.en: Ah, mendok sai.
sentences.zh: 啊，真麻烦（mendok sai）。

sentences.en: If you're bilingual or you're learning a new language, you get what Jennifer experienced.
sentences.zh: 如果你是双语者或者正在学习一门新语言，你就能理解詹妮弗的感受。

sentences.en: The joy of discovering a phrase that helps you perfectly encapsulate a feeling or an experience.
sentences.zh: 发现一个能完美概括某种感觉或经历的短语，那种快乐是无与伦比的。

sentences.en: The phrase brings an entire world with it.
sentences.zh: 这个短语带来了一个完整的世界。

sentences.en: Its context, its flavor, its culture.
sentences.zh: 它的语境、它的韵味、它的文化。

sentences.en: Today, we explore the many facets of this idea.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨这个概念的多个层面。

sentences.en: Languages are not just tools to describe the world.
sentences.zh: 语言不仅仅是描述世界的工具。

sentences.en: They are ways of seeing the world.
sentences.zh: 它们是看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: The categorization that language provides to you becomes real, becomes psychologically real.
sentences.zh: 语言为你提供的分类方式会变得真实，在心理层面上变得真实。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: How the languages we speak shape the way we think and why the words we use are always in flux.
sentences.zh: 我们所说的语言如何塑造我们的思维方式，以及为什么我们使用的词汇总是在不断变化。

sentences.en: My guest today is, why don't I let her introduce herself?
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是……不如让她自己介绍一下？

sentences.en: The way to say my name properly in Russian is Kaleria Romanovna Boroditskaya.
sentences.zh: 我名字的俄语正确读法是卡莱里亚·罗曼诺夫娜·博罗迪茨卡娅。
zh_words: 卡莱里亚·罗曼诺夫娜·博罗迪茨

sentences.en: So I don't make people say that.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会强迫别人那样叫我。

sentences.en: Well, that's kind of you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你真体贴。

sentences.en: In the English-speaking world, she goes by Lera Boroditsky.
sentences.zh: 在英语世界里，她叫莱拉·博罗迪茨基。

sentences.en: Lera is a cognitive science professor at the University of California, San Diego.
sentences.zh: 莱拉是加州大学圣地亚哥分校的认知科学教授。

sentences.en: Long before she began researching languages as a professor, foreign languages loomed large in her life.
sentences.zh: 早在她成为教授开始研究语言之前，外语就在她的生活中占据了重要地位。

sentences.en: When she was 12, her family came to the United States from the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 12岁时，她随家人从苏联来到美国。

sentences.en: My family is Jewish, and we left as refugees.
sentences.zh: 我的家庭是犹太裔，我们是以难民身份离开的。

sentences.en: I decided it was very important for me to learn English because I'd always been a very verbal kid,
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得学习英语对我来说非常重要，因为我一直是个很健谈的孩子，

sentences.en: and I was always the person who recited poems in front of the school and led assemblies and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我总是那个在学校里朗诵诗歌、主持集会之类活动的人。

sentences.en: And to arrive in a new place where you can't tell a joke and can't express an idea,
sentences.zh: 来到一个新地方，却无法讲笑话，也无法表达想法，

sentences.en: oh, it's just really painful because you feel like your whole self is hiding inside and no one can see it.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真的非常痛苦，因为你会觉得整个自我都藏在里面，没人能看见。

sentences.en: And so I set myself the goal that I would learn English in a year,
sentences.zh: 所以我给自己定下目标，要在一年内学会英语，

sentences.en: and I wouldn't speak Russian to anyone for that whole first year.
sentences.zh: 而且在那第一年里，我不跟任何人说俄语。

sentences.en: And I did that.
sentences.zh: 我做到了。

sentences.en: Lera now tries to understand languages spoken all over the world.
sentences.zh: 莱拉现在致力于研究世界各地的语言。

sentences.en: She once visited an Aboriginal community in Northern Australia and found the language they spoke forced her mind to work in new ways.
sentences.zh: 她曾访问过澳大利亚北部的一个原住民社区，发现他们所说的语言迫使她的思维以新的方式运作。

sentences.en: Just saying hello was difficult.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是打个招呼都很困难。

sentences.en: I had this wonderful opportunity to work with my colleague Alice Gaby in this community called Pomparao on Cape York.
sentences.zh: 我有幸与同事爱丽丝·加比在约克角一个叫庞帕劳的社区工作。

sentences.en: And what's cool about languages like the languages spoken in Pomparao is that they don't use words like left and right,
sentences.zh: 像庞帕劳语这类语言的酷之处在于，它们不使用“左”和“右”这样的词，

sentences.en: and instead everything is placed in cardinal directions, like north, south, east, and weSt.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是一切都用方位词来定位，比如北、南、东、西。

sentences.en: So the way you say hi in Cook Tire is to say, which way are you heading?
sentences.zh: 所以在库克泰尔语中打招呼的方式是问：“你要去哪儿？”

sentences.en: And the answer should be north, northeast in the far distance.
sentences.zh: 回答应该是：“去远处的东北方。”

sentences.en: How about you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: So quite literally to get past hello, you have to know which way you're heading.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，想要打完招呼，你必须知道自己正朝哪个方向走。

sentences.en: And in fact, speakers of languages like this have been shown to orient extremely well,
sentences.zh: 事实上，研究表明，这类语言的使用者方向感极好，

sentences.en: much better than we used to think humans could.
sentences.zh: 远比我们过去认为人类所能达到的程度要好。

sentences.en: We always knew that certain species of animals had abilities to orient that we thought were better than human,
sentences.zh: 我们一直知道某些动物物种拥有我们认为优于人类的定向能力，

sentences.en: and we always had some biological excuse for why we couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 而且我们总是为自己做不到这一点找一些生物学上的借口。

sentences.en: We'd say, oh, well, we don't have magnets in our beaks or in our scales or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我们会说，哦，好吧，我们的喙或鳞片里又没有磁铁之类的东西。

sentences.en: But it turns out humans can stay oriented really, really well,
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，人类完全可以保持非常、非常好的方向感，

sentences.en: provided that their language and culture requires them to keep track of this information.
sentences.zh: 前提是他们的语言和文化要求他们必须掌握这些信息。

sentences.en: I understand that if you're in a picnic with someone from this community
sentences.zh: 我理解，如果你和这个社区的人一起野餐的话

sentences.en: and you notice an ant climbing up someone's left leg,
sentences.zh: 当你注意到有只蚂蚁正爬上某人的左腿时，

sentences.en: it wouldn't make a lot of sense to tell that person, look, there's an ant on your left leg.
sentences.zh: 告诉那个人“看，你左腿上有只蚂蚁”其实没什么意义。

sentences.en: Well, there may not be a word for left to refer to a left leg.
sentences.zh: 嗯，可能根本就没有用来指代“左腿”的“左”这个词。

sentences.en: In a lot of languages, there isn't.
sentences.zh: 在很多语言中，确实没有。

sentences.en: So you might say there's an ant on your northwest leg.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会说，你西北方向的那条腿上有只蚂蚁。

sentences.en: The fun example I give my students is imagine playing the hokey pokey in a language like this.
sentences.zh: 我给学生举过一个有趣的例子，想象一下用这种语言玩“Hokey Pokey”舞蹈游戏。

sentences.en: You know, there's no left leg or right leg.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有左腿或右腿之分。

sentences.en: As soon as you move the leg, it becomes a different leg.
sentences.zh: 一旦你移动了那条腿，它就变成了另一条腿。

sentences.en: So you may start with moving your southwest leg in,
sentences.zh: 所以你可能开始时是移动你的西南腿向内，

sentences.en: but then you have to move your northeast leg out.
sentences.zh: 但接着你必须移动你的东北腿向外。

sentences.en: You put your southwest leg in and you shake it all about.
sentences.zh: 你把西南腿伸进去，然后摇晃它。

sentences.en: You do the hokey pokey and you turn yourself around.
sentences.zh: 你跳着Hokey Pokey，然后转个身。

sentences.en: That's what it's all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的全部精髓。

sentences.en: So I find that I'm often directionally and navigationally challenged when I'm driving around
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在开车时，方向感和导航能力往往很差，

sentences.en: and I often get my east-west mixed up with my left-right for reasons I have never been able to fathom.
sentences.zh: 而且我经常把东西南北和左右搞混，原因我至今无法理解。

sentences.en: But if I understand correctly, I would be completely at sea if I visited this aboriginal community in Australia
sentences.zh: 但如果我理解得没错，如果我访问澳大利亚的那个原住民社区，我肯定会彻底迷失方向，

sentences.en: because I have often absolutely no idea where I am or where I'm going.
sentences.zh: 因为我经常完全不知道自己在哪里，或者要去哪里。

sentences.en: Well, you would be at sea at first, but actually it's something that's not so hard to learn.
sentences.zh: 嗯，起初你会迷失方向，但实际上这并不是很难学。

sentences.en: Many people have this intuition that, oh, I could never learn that.
sentences.zh: 很多人有一种直觉，觉得“哦，我永远学不会那个”。

sentences.en: I could never survive in a community like this.
sentences.zh: “我永远无法在这样的社区里生存。”

sentences.en: But actually that's exactly how people in those communities come to stay oriented is that they learn it, right?
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这正是那些社区的人保持方向感的方式，他们学会了它，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to do it in order to fit into the culture and to speak the language.
sentences.zh: 你必须这样做才能融入文化并说这种语言。

sentences.en: I had this cool experience when I was there.
sentences.zh: 我在那里时有过一次很酷的经历。

sentences.en: You know, I was trying to stay oriented because people were treating me like I was pretty stupid for not being oriented.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时努力保持方向感，因为人们觉得我因为没有方向感而显得很笨。

sentences.en: And that hurt.
sentences.zh: 那让我很受伤。

sentences.en: And so I was trying to keep track of which was which.
sentences.zh: 所以我努力去追踪哪个方向是哪个方向。

sentences.en: And one day I was walking along and I was just staring at the ground.
sentences.zh: 有一天我走着走着，只是盯着地面看。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden I noticed that there was a new window that had popped up in my mind.
sentences.zh: 突然间，我注意到脑海中弹出了一个新窗口。

sentences.en: And it was like a little bird's eye view of the landscape that I was walking through.
sentences.zh: 就像是我正走过的这片土地的鸟瞰图。

sentences.en: And I was a little red dot that was moving across the landscape.
sentences.zh: 而我是一个正在这片土地上移动的小红点。

sentences.en: And then when I turned, this little window stayed locked on the landscape, but it turned in my mind's eye.
sentences.zh: 当我转弯时，这个小窗口锁定在地形上，但在我的脑海中它转动了。

sentences.en: And as soon as I saw that happen, I thought, oh, this makes it so much easier.
sentences.zh: 一旦我看到这种情况发生，我就想，哦，这让事情变得容易多了。

sentences.en: Now I can stay oriented.
sentences.zh: 现在我可以保持方向感了。

sentences.en: And I kind of sheepishly confessed this to someone there.
sentences.zh: 我有些羞怯地向那里的人坦白了这件事。

sentences.en: I said, you know, this weird thing happened.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，发生了一件奇怪的事。

sentences.en: I saw this bird's eye view and I was this little red dot.
sentences.zh: 我看到了这个鸟瞰图，而我就是那个小红点。

sentences.en: And they said, well, of course, how else would you do it?
sentences.zh: 他们说，嗯，当然了，不然你还能怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: What was remarkable for me was that my brain figured out a really good solution to the problem after a week of trying.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，了不起的是，我的大脑在尝试了一周后，为这个问题找到了一个非常好的解决方案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think it's something that is quite easy for humans to learn if you just have a reason to want to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果人类有理由想要学习，这其实是很容易学会的。

sentences.en: Time is another concept that is also central to the way we see and describe the world.
sentences.zh: 时间是另一个对我们观察和描述世界方式至关重要的概念。

sentences.en: And you've conducted experiments that explore how different conceptions of time in different languages shape the way we think about the world and shape the way we think about stories.
sentences.zh: 你进行过一些实验，探讨不同语言中对时间的不同构想如何塑造我们思考世界的方式，以及我们思考故事的方式。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说呢？

sentences.en: One thing that we've noticed is this idea of time, of course, is very highly constructed by our minds and our brains.
sentences.zh: 我们注意到的一件事是，时间这个概念，当然，是由我们的思想和大脑高度构建出来的。

sentences.en: So you can't see time.
sentences.zh: 所以你看不见时间。

sentences.en: You can't touch time.
sentences.zh: 你摸不到时间。

sentences.en: You can't smell or taste time.
sentences.zh: 你闻不到也尝不出时间。

sentences.en: But it is a completely crucial part of the human experience.
sentences.zh: 但它是人类体验中至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Of course, you also can't experience anything outside of time.
sentences.zh: 当然，你也不可能体验到时间之外的任何事物。

sentences.en: It is the very fabric, the very core of your experience.
sentences.zh: 它是你体验的基石，是核心所在。

sentences.en: So the question for us has been, how do we build these ideas?
sentences.zh: 所以对我们来说，问题一直是：我们是如何构建这些概念的？

sentences.en: And it's not just about how we think about time.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅关乎我们如何思考时间。

sentences.en: It's how we think about anything that's abstract, that's beyond our physical senses.
sentences.zh: 这关乎我们如何思考任何抽象的、超出我们物理感官的事物。

sentences.en: And one thing that we've noticed is that around the world, people rely on space to organize time.
sentences.zh: 我们注意到的一件事是，在世界各地，人们都依赖空间来组织时间。

sentences.en: So, for example, for English speakers, people who read from left to right, time tends to flow from left to right.
sentences.zh: 例如，对于英语使用者来说，从左向右阅读的人，时间往往是从左向右流动的。

sentences.en: So earlier things are on the left, later things are on the right.
sentences.zh: 所以较早的事情在左边，较晚的事情在右边。

sentences.en: If I give you a bunch of pictures to lay out and say, this is telling you some kind of story and they're disorganized,
sentences.zh: 如果我给你一堆图片让你排列，并说这在讲述某种故事，而它们是杂乱无章的，

sentences.en: when an English speaker organizes those pictures, they'll organize them from left to right.
sentences.zh: 当英语使用者整理这些图片时，他们会从左到右排列。

sentences.en: But if I give that same story to a Hebrew or an Arabic speaker, they would organize it from right to left.
sentences.zh: 但如果我把同样的故事给希伯来语或阿拉伯语使用者，他们会从右到左排列。

sentences.en: That is the direction of writing in Hebrew and Arabic, going from right to left.
sentences.zh: 这就是希伯来语和阿拉伯语的书写方向，从右到左。

sentences.en: But time doesn't have to flow with respect to the body.
sentences.zh: 但时间并不一定要相对于身体流动。

sentences.en: So to go back to the example we were just talking about, people who don't use words like left and right,
sentences.zh: 回到我们刚才讨论的例子，那些不使用“左”和“右”这类词的人，

sentences.en: when I gave those picture stories to Kuk Tire speakers who use north, south, east, and west,
sentences.zh: 当我把那些图片故事给使用“北、南、东、西”的库克泰耶尔语使用者时，

sentences.en: they organized the cards from east to weSt.
sentences.zh: 他们从东向西排列这些卡片。

sentences.en: And so what that means is if someone was sitting facing south, they would lay out the story from left to right.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果有人面朝南坐着，他们会从左到右排列故事。

sentences.en: But if they're sitting facing north, they would lay out the story from right to left.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们面朝北坐着，他们会从右到左排列故事。

sentences.en: And if they're facing east, they would make the cards come toward them, toward the body.
sentences.zh: 如果他们面朝东，他们会让卡片朝向他们自己，朝向身体方向。

sentences.en: So that's an example of how languages and cultures construct how we use space to organize time,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是语言和文化如何构建我们利用空间来组织时间的例子，

sentences.en: to organize this very abstract thing that's otherwise kind of hard to get our hands on and think about.
sentences.zh: 用来组织这种非常抽象、否则很难把握和思考的事物。

sentences.en: If languages are shaped by the way people see the world, but they also shape how people see the world,
sentences.zh: 如果语言是由人们观察世界的方式所塑造的，但它们同时也塑造了人们观察世界的方式，

sentences.en: what does this mean for people who are bilingual?
sentences.zh: 这对双语者意味着什么？

sentences.en: If you can speak more than one language, does this mean that you're also simultaneously
sentences.zh: 如果你能说不止一种语言，这是否意味着你同时也

sentences.en: and constantly shifting in your mind between different worldviews?
sentences.zh: 在脑海中不断地在不同的世界观之间切换？

sentences.en: That's a wonderful question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的问题。

sentences.en: So one possibility for bilinguals would be that they just have two different minds inside, right?
sentences.zh: 所以双语者的一种可能性是，他们的内心只是拥有两个不同的思维，对吧？

sentences.en: So one skull, but two different minds, and you shift from one to the other.
sentences.zh: 也就是同一个大脑，但有两个不同的思维，你会在两者之间切换。

sentences.en: Another possibility is that it's a fully integrated mind,
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是，这是一个完全整合的思维，

sentences.en: and it just incorporates ideas and distinctions from both languages,
sentences.zh: 它只是融合了两种语言中的观点和区别，

sentences.en: or from many languages if you speak more than two.
sentences.zh: 如果你会说两种以上的语言，它甚至融合了多种语言的观点。

sentences.en: What turns out to be the case is that it's something in between,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，情况介于两者之间，

sentences.en: that bilinguals don't really turn off the languages they're not using when they're not using them.
sentences.zh: 双语者在不使用某种语言时，并不会真正将其“关闭”。

sentences.en: So even if I'm speaking English, the distinctions that I've learned in speaking Russian, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以即使我在说英语，比如我在学习俄语时学到的那些区别，

sentences.en: are still active in my mind to some extent.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，它们在我的大脑中依然是活跃的。

sentences.en: But they're more active if I'm actually speaking Russian.
sentences.zh: 但如果我真的在说俄语，它们会更加活跃。

sentences.en: So bilinguals are kind of this in-between case where they can't quite turn off their other languages,
sentences.zh: 所以双语者处于这种中间状态，他们无法完全关闭其他语言，

sentences.en: but they become more prominent, more salient when you're actually speaking the language or surrounded by the language.
sentences.zh: 但当你真正说某种语言或置身于该语言环境时，这些语言会变得更加突出、更加显著。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about a debate that's raged in your field for many years.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈你们领域争论了多年的一个话题。

sentences.en: There are many scholars who would say,
sentences.zh: 有很多学者会说，

sentences.en: look, yes, you do see small differences between speakers of different languages,
sentences.zh: 看，没错，你确实能看到不同语言使用者之间存在细微差异，

sentences.en: but these differences are not really significant.
sentences.zh: 但这些差异并不真正重要。

sentences.en: They're really small.
sentences.zh: 它们真的很小。

sentences.en: How big are the differences that we're talking about,
sentences.zh: 我们所说的差异到底有多大，

sentences.en: and how big do you think the implications are for the way we see the world?
sentences.zh: 你认为这对我们看待世界的方式有多大的影响？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there are some differences that are as big as you can possibly measure.
sentences.zh: 有些差异大到你无法想象。

sentences.en: For example, when we started talking about navigation,
sentences.zh: 例如，当我们开始谈论导航时，

sentences.en: that's an example where a five-year-old in a culture that uses words like north, south, east, and west
sentences.zh: 这是一个例子：在一种使用“北、南、东、西”这类词汇的文化中，一个五岁的孩子

sentences.en: can point southeast without hesitation.
sentences.zh: 可以毫不犹豫地指出东南方向。

sentences.en: They know which way is which.
sentences.zh: 他们知道哪个方向是哪个方向。

sentences.en: And very competent adults of our culture can't do that.
sentences.zh: 而我们文化中非常有能力的成年人却做不到这一点。

sentences.en: So that's a measurement difference of 100% of performance.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个表现上百分之百的测量差异。

sentences.en: There's not a bigger difference you could find than 100% of the measurement space.
sentences.zh: 在测量空间里，你找不到比这更大的差异了。

sentences.en: You also see huge differences in other domains like number.
sentences.zh: 你在数字等其他领域也能看到巨大的差异。

sentences.en: So some languages don't have number words.
sentences.zh: 有些语言没有数字词汇。

sentences.en: And if you don't have a word for exactly seven,
sentences.zh: 如果你没有一个确切表示“七”的词，

sentences.en: it actually becomes very, very hard to keep track of exactly seven.
sentences.zh: 要准确记录“七”的数量实际上会变得非常非常困难。

sentences.en: And that is an example of a simple feature of language, number words,
sentences.zh: 这就是语言的一个简单特征——数字词汇，

sentences.en: acting as a transformative stepping stone to a whole domain of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 它成为了通往整个知识领域的变革性垫脚石。

sentences.en: Of course, if you can't keep track of exactly seven, you can't count,
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你无法准确记录“七”，你就无法计数，

sentences.en: you're also not going to do algebra, you're not going to do trigonometry,
sentences.zh: 你也无法进行代数运算，无法进行三角函数运算，

sentences.en: you're not going to do any of the things that are seen as a foundation of our technological society.
sentences.zh: 你无法完成任何被视为我们技术社会基础的事情。

sentences.en: So that, again, is a huge difference.
sentences.zh: 所以，这又是一个巨大的差异。

sentences.en: So in terms of the size of differences, there are certainly effects that are really, really big.
sentences.zh: 因此，就差异的大小而言，确实存在一些非常非常大的影响。

sentences.en: But things can be important not just because they're big.
sentences.zh: 但事物之所以重要，不仅仅是因为它们很大。

sentences.en: They can be small differences but important in other ways.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是微小的差异，但在其他方面却很重要。

sentences.en: So, for example, grammatical gender.
sentences.zh: 比如，语法性别。

sentences.en: Because grammatical gender applies to all nouns in your language,
sentences.zh: 因为语法性别适用于你语言中的所有名词，

sentences.en: that means that language is shaping the way you think about everything that can be named by a noun.
sentences.zh: 这意味着语言正在塑造你对所有能用名词命名的事物的看法。

sentences.en: Well, that's an incredibly large set of things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是一个极其庞大的事物集合。

sentences.en: So that's a very broad effect of language.
sentences.zh: 所以这是语言产生的一种非常广泛的影响。

sentences.en: So to give you a very quick wrap-up is that some effects are big,
sentences.zh: 简单总结一下，有些影响很大，

sentences.en: but even when the effects aren't big, they can be interesting or important for other reasons,
sentences.zh: 但即使影响不大，它们也可能因为其他原因而变得有趣或重要，

sentences.en: either because they're very broad or because they apply to things that we think are really important in our culture.
sentences.zh: 要么是因为它们非常广泛，要么是因为它们适用于我们文化中认为非常重要的事物。

sentences.en: Languages orient us to the world.
sentences.zh: 语言引导我们认识世界。

sentences.en: They shape our place in it.
sentences.zh: 它们塑造了我们在其中的位置。

sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将进一步深入探讨性别在不同语言中是如何运作的，

sentences.en: and the pervasive effects that words can play in our lives.
sentences.zh: 以及词汇在我们生活中可能产生的普遍影响。

sentences.en: changes the way that speakers of different languages think about those concepts.
sentences.zh: 是如何改变不同语言的使用者对这些概念的思考方式的。

sentences.en: Actually, one of the first people to notice or suggest that this might be the case
sentences.zh: 事实上，最早注意到或提出这一点的人之一，

sentences.en: was a Russian linguist, Roman Jakobsen.
sentences.zh: 是一位俄语语言学家，罗曼·雅各布森。

sentences.zh: 他首先让讲俄语的学生将一周中的每一天进行拟人化。

sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，一周中不同的日子有不同的性别。

sentences.zh: 他注意到，当人们试图表现得像周一时，他们会表现得

sentences.en: Понедельник.
sentences.zh: 周一（俄语）。

sentences.zh: 而当他们试图表现得像周三时，他们会表现得像个女人。

sentences.en: Среда.
sentences.zh: 周三（俄语）。

sentences.en: Which accords with grammatical gender in Russian.
sentences.zh: 这与俄语中的语法性别相吻合。

sentences.zh: 因此，他提出，可能正是这些被随意分配的语法性别，

sentences.en: are actually changing the way people think about these days of the week and maybe all kinds
sentences.zh: 实际上正在改变人们对这些日子以及可能所有其他

sentences.en: of other things that are named by nouns.
sentences.zh: 用名词命名的事物的看法。

sentences.en: So, we've done a lot of studies looking at how speakers of Spanish and German and Russian
sentences.zh: 所以，我们做了很多研究，观察讲西班牙语、德语和俄语的人

sentences.en: actually think about objects that have opposite grammatical genders.
sentences.zh: 是如何思考那些具有相反语法性别的物体的。

sentences.zh: 以“桥”这个词为例，如果它在你的语言中是阴性的。

sentences.zh: 你更有可能说桥是美丽而优雅的。

sentences.en: And if the word bridge is masculine in your language, you're more likely to say that bridges

sentences.en: are strong and long and towering.
sentences.zh: 是坚固、漫长且高耸的。

sentences.zh: 这些是更具刻板印象的阳性词汇。

sentences.en: And of course, you always have to wonder, well, could it be that speakers of these different
sentences.zh: 当然，你总是会想，会不会是因为这些不同语言的使用者

sentences.en: languages are actually seeing different kinds of bridges?
sentences.zh: 实际上看到的桥梁种类不同呢？

sentences.en: So, maybe they're saying bridges are beautiful and elegant, not because they're grammatically
sentences.zh: 所以，也许他们说桥是美丽而优雅的，不是因为它们在语言中是语法上的

sentences.en: feminine in the language, but because the bridges they have are, in fact, more beautiful and
sentences.zh: 阴性，而是因为他们拥有的桥梁实际上确实更美丽、更

sentences.zh: 优雅。

sentences.en: We call this language gumbuzzi.
sentences.zh: 我们把这种语言称为“Gumbuzzi”。

sentences.en: And we teach them, for example, to say that bridges and apples and all kinds of other things

sentences.zh: 以及意大利语和德语的双语使用者，解释为什么事物具有

sentences.zh: 如果你是这些语言中某种语言的单语使用者，你很可能会说

sentences.zh: 所以，这些使用者已经从他们的语言中内化了这个想法，并且认为这是正确的。

sentences.zh: 写在那张纸上，就会产生那种错觉。

sentences.en: of doing it.
sentences.zh: 同样的理念。

sentences.en: Language was talk.
sentences.zh: 语言就是交谈。

sentences.en: When language was like that, of course, it changed a lot, fast, because once you said it,
sentences.zh: 当语言是那样时，它当然变化得非常快，因为一旦你说出口，

sentences.en: it was gone.
sentences.zh: 它就消失了。

sentences.en: And if people heard the sounds a little differently and produced them a little differently, if
sentences.zh: 如果人们对声音的听感略有不同，发音也略有不同，

sentences.en: there were new meanings of words, very quickly, whatever the original meaning was wouldn't
sentences.zh: 如果词语有了新含义，那么很快，无论最初的含义是什么，都不会

sentences.en: be remembered.
sentences.zh: 被记住了。

sentences.en: There was no such thing as looking up what it originally meant.
sentences.zh: 根本没有查证它最初含义这回事。

sentences.en: And so language changed, just like the clouds and the sky.
sentences.zh: 因此语言不断变化，就像天上的云彩一样。

sentences.en: But then you start writing things down, and you're in a whole new land, because once things
sentences.zh: 但当你开始把事情写下来时，你就进入了一个全新的天地，因为一旦事情

sentences.en: are sitting there written on that piece of paper, there's that illusion.
sentences.zh: 安安静静地写在那张纸上，就会产生一种错觉。

sentences.en: And it really is an illusion that what language is is something that sits still.
sentences.zh: 语言是一种静止不变的东西，这确实是一种错觉。

sentences.en: There's a way of speaking right.
sentences.zh: 有一种所谓的“正确”说话方式。

sentences.en: And the way you speak right is not by speaking the way the people around you in your life speak,
sentences.zh: 而这种“正确”的说话方式，并不是通过模仿你生活中周围人的说话方式来实现的，

sentences.en: but by speaking the way the language is as it sits there, all nice and pretty on that piece
sentences.zh: 而是通过模仿那种存在于纸面上、静止不动、整齐美观的语言，

sentences.en: of paper where its reality exists.
sentences.zh: 因为那才是它现实存在的地方。

sentences.en: Would it be possible to use what we have learned about how words and languages evolve to potentially
sentences.zh: 我们是否有可能利用所学的关于词汇和语言演变的知识，来推测

sentences.en: write what a dictionary might look like in 50 years or 100 years?
sentences.zh: 50年或100年后的词典会是什么样子？

sentences.en: You could have fun doing such a thing.
sentences.zh: 做这样的事情会很有趣。

sentences.en: The fact is that language change can always go in one of many directions.
sentences.zh: 事实是，语言的变化总是可能朝多个方向发展。

sentences.en: There's a chance element to it.
sentences.zh: 其中存在随机因素。

sentences.en: So you can't know how the words are going to come out, but you can take good guesses.
sentences.zh: 所以你无法预知词汇最终会变成什么样，但你可以做出合理的猜测。

sentences.en: You know, endings are going to tend to drop off.
sentences.zh: 你知道，词尾往往会趋向于脱落。

sentences.en: So if you took a bunch of those tendencies, you could make up, say, the English of 50 years from now.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你掌握了这些趋势，你或许就能编撰出50年后的英语。

sentences.en: But some of the things would just be complete chance.
sentences.zh: 但其中一些变化纯粹是偶然的。

sentences.en: You would never know, for example, that give you an example I've actually been thinking
sentences.zh: 你永远无法预料，举个例子，我一直在思考

sentences.en: about women under about 30 in the United States, when they're excited or they're trying to
sentences.zh: 美国30岁以下的女性，当她们感到兴奋或试图

sentences.en: underline a point, putting a at the end of things.
sentences.zh: 强调某个观点时，会在句末加上一个“a”。

sentences.en: And so somebody will say, well, who was it who you thought was going to give you this present?
sentences.zh: 比如有人会说：“你以为是谁要送你这个礼物？”

sentences.en: You.
sentences.zh: “你啊。”

sentences.en: And I mean, really, it sounds exactly like that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，听起来确实就是那样。

sentences.en: I know what is there or something along the lines of babe.
sentences.zh: 我知道那里有什么，或者类似于“宝贝”之类的词。

sentences.en: And as odd as that sounds, I can guarantee you, if you watch any TV show with women under
sentences.zh: 虽然听起来很奇怪，但我敢保证，如果你看任何有年轻女性参与的电视节目，

sentences.en: a certain age or if you just go out on an American street and listen, you'll find that that's
sentences.zh: 或者走在美国街头留心听一下，你会发现这是一种

sentences.en: a new kind of exclamatory particle.
sentences.zh: 新型的感叹助词。

sentences.en: That is the most random thing.
sentences.zh: 这真是最随机的事情了。

sentences.en: And I would really guess that in a few decades, men will be doing it, too.
sentences.zh: 我敢猜过不了几十年，男性也会开始这样说。

sentences.en: Those sorts of things tend to start with women.
sentences.zh: 这类事情往往是从女性开始的。

sentences.en: You couldn't have predicted this.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法预测这一点。

sentences.en: I know, move.
sentences.zh: 我知道，走吧。

sentences.en: You can't know, but you can certainly know that if we could listen to people 50 years
sentences.zh: 你无法预知未来，但你肯定知道，如果我们能听到50年后人们的谈话，

sentences.en: from now, they'd sound odd.
sentences.zh: 他们听起来会很奇怪。

sentences.en: Something new will have started by then, just like if we listen to people in 1971, they
sentences.zh: 到那时一定会有新的东西出现，就像我们听1971年人们的谈话，

sentences.en: sound odd in that they don't say like as much as we do.
sentences.zh: 他们听起来很奇怪，因为他们不像我们这样频繁使用“like”。

sentences.en: That hadn't started then.
sentences.zh: 那时还没开始流行。

sentences.en: Imagine how we would sound to them if they could hear us.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果他们能听到我们说话，会觉得我们有多奇怪。

sentences.en: If you're so upset about it, maybe you can think of a way to help her.
sentences.zh: 如果你对此感到如此不安，也许你可以想办法帮帮她。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, lots of people blow off steam about something they think is wrong, but very few
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人会对他们认为错误的事情发泄不满，但很少

sentences.en: people are willing to get involved and do something about it.
sentences.zh: 有人愿意参与其中并采取行动。

sentences.en: I'm willing to get involved.
sentences.zh: 我愿意参与。

sentences.en: So all this raises a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切引出了一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: You know, we spend years teaching children about how to use language correctly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们花了好几年时间教孩子们如何正确使用语言。

sentences.en: As someone who works in media, I often find that people who can write well are often people
sentences.zh: 作为一名媒体从业者，我经常发现，擅长写作的人通常也是

sentences.en: who know how to think well.
sentences.zh: 擅长思考的人。

sentences.en: So I often equate clarity of writing with clarity of thought.
sentences.zh: 所以我常把写作的清晰度与思维的清晰度等同起来。

sentences.en: How do you balance the imperative of teaching correct usage, which I think is probably important,
sentences.zh: 你如何平衡“教授正确用法”（我认为这可能很重要）的必要性，

sentences.en: with the reality that this edifice that you're teaching is constantly crumbling?
sentences.zh: 与“你所教授的这座大厦正在不断崩塌”这一现实之间的关系？

sentences.en: It's a matter of fashion, pure and simple.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是时尚问题，简单明了。

sentences.en: People do need to be taught what the socially acceptable forms are.
sentences.zh: 人们确实需要被教导什么是社会可接受的形式。

sentences.en: But what we should teach is not that the good way is logical and the way that you're comfortable
sentences.zh: 但我们不应该教导说，那种“正确”的方式是合乎逻辑的，而你习惯的

sentences.en: doing it is illogical.
sentences.zh: 表达方式是不合逻辑的。

sentences.en: It should just be here is the natural way.
sentences.zh: 应该只是说：这是自然的方式。

sentences.en: Then there's some things that you're supposed to do in public because that's the way it is,
sentences.zh: 然后，有些事情你必须在公共场合做，因为事实就是如此，

sentences.en: whether it's fair or not.
sentences.zh: 无论这是否公平。

sentences.en: You can even teach people to have a little bit of fun with the artifice.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以教人们从这种人为的规则中找点乐子。

sentences.en: But it's exactly like it was maybe about 20 years ago that somebody, a girlfriend I had,
sentences.zh: 这就像大约20年前，我当时的女朋友

sentences.en: told me that if I wore pants that had little vertical pleats up near the waist,
sentences.zh: 告诉我，如果我穿腰部有小褶皱的裤子，

sentences.en: then I was conveying that I was kind of past it.
sentences.zh: 就是在传达一种“我已经过时了”的信息。

sentences.en: That was somehow a dad's fashion and that I should start wearing flat fronted pants.
sentences.zh: 那不知怎么成了老爸辈的时尚，我应该开始穿平口裤。

sentences.en: That is utterly arbitrary that those little slits in American society look elderly.
sentences.zh: 在美国社会中，那些小褶皱看起来显老，这完全是武断的。

sentences.en: But for various chance reasons, that's what those slits came to mean.
sentences.zh: 但由于各种偶然原因，那些褶皱就有了那样的含义。

sentences.en: So I started wearing flat fronted pants.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始穿平口裤了。

sentences.en: That is exactly why you should say fewer books instead of less books in some situations.
sentences.zh: 这正是为什么在某些情况下你应该说“fewer books”而不是“less books”。

sentences.en: And yes, Billy and I went to the store rather than the perfectly natural Billy and me went to the store.
sentences.zh: 还有，说“Billy and I went to the store”而不是极其自然的“Billy and me went to the store”。

sentences.en: Sometimes you just have to suck it up.
sentences.zh: 有时候你只能忍受。

sentences.en: But I think that we should learn not to listen to people using natural language as committing errors
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们应该学会不要把使用自然语言的人视为犯错，

sentences.en: because there's no such thing as making a mistake in your language
sentences.zh: 因为在语言中根本不存在犯错这一说，

sentences.en: if a critical mass of other people speaking your language are doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 只要有足够多的人都在使用同样的表达方式。

sentences.en: You make the case that concerns over the misuse of language might actually be one of the last places
sentences.zh: 你提出一个观点，即对语言误用的担忧，实际上可能是人们

sentences.en: where people can publicly express prejudice and class differences.
sentences.zh: 公开表达偏见和阶级差异的最后阵地之一。

sentences.en: And as you point out, it's not just that people feel that a word is being misused.
sentences.zh: 正如你指出的，人们不仅仅是觉得某个词被误用了。

sentences.en: They often feel angry about it.
sentences.zh: 他们往往对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And you think this anger is actually telling.
sentences.zh: 而你认为这种愤怒其实很有深意。

sentences.en: Yeah, I really do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实这么认为。

sentences.en: I think that the tone that many people use when they're complaining that somebody says,
sentences.zh: 我认为许多人在抱怨别人说“Billy and me went to the store”时，

sentences.en: Billy and me went to the store,
sentences.zh: 所使用的那种语气，

sentences.en: is a little bit incommensurate with the significance of the issue.
sentences.zh: 与这个问题的重要性有些不相称。

sentences.en: And I can't help surmising that part of it is that the educated American has been taught,
sentences.zh: 我不禁推测，部分原因是受过教育的美国人被教导过，

sentences.en: and often well, that you're not supposed to look down on people because of gender,
sentences.zh: 而且往往教得很好，即你不应该因为性别、

sentences.en: because of race, because of ability.
sentences.zh: 种族或能力而看不起别人。

sentences.en: But might we allow that there's probably a part of all human beings that wants to look down on somebody else?
sentences.zh: 但我们是否可以承认，人类内心深处可能都有一部分想要看不起别人？

sentences.en: What a cynical thing to say, but that doesn't mean that it might not be true.
sentences.zh: 这话听起来很愤世嫉俗，但这并不意味着它不是真的。

sentences.en: And if that is true, then the educated person can look down on people who say,
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，那么受过教育的人就可以看不起那些说

sentences.en: Billy and me went to the store or who are using literally quote unquote wrong
sentences.zh: “Billy and me went to the store”或使用“literally”等“错误”用法的人，

sentences.en: and condemn them in the kinds of terms that once were ordinary for condemning black people or women or what have you.
sentences.zh: 并用曾经用来谴责黑人、女性或其他群体的那种措辞来谴责他们。

sentences.en: So I just think that it's something we need to check ourselves for.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们需要反思一下自己。

sentences.en: It might irritate you slightly to hear somebody say something like,
sentences.zh: 听到别人说类似“I need less books”而不是“fewer books”的话，

sentences.en: I need less books instead of fewer books.
sentences.zh: 可能会让你感到些许恼火。

sentences.en: But does a person who says that really deserve the kind of sneering condemnation that you often see?
sentences.zh: 但说这话的人真的值得你经常表现出的那种冷嘲热讽吗？

sentences.en: There's a lowlier part of our nature that grammar allows us to vent in the absence of other ways to do it
sentences.zh: 我们人性中卑微的一面，在缺乏其他发泄渠道的情况下，语法给了我们一个宣泄口，

sentences.en: that have not been available for some decades, for a lot of us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们很多人来说，已经几十年没有过这样的机会了。

sentences.en: One of the ultimate messages I took from your work is that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我从你的作品中领悟到的终极信息之一是，你知道，

sentences.en: we can choose to have languages that are alive or languages that are dead.
sentences.zh: 我们可以选择拥有鲜活的语言，还是死去的语言。

sentences.en: And dead languages never change.
sentences.zh: 而死去的语言永远不会改变。

sentences.en: And some of us might prefer those.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能更喜欢后者。

sentences.en: But if you prefer life, the unpredictability of life,
sentences.zh: 但如果你热爱生命，热爱生命的不可预测性，

sentences.en: then living languages in many ways are much more fun.
sentences.zh: 那么活着的语言在很多方面要有趣得多。

sentences.en: Language is a parade.
sentences.zh: 语言就像一场游行。

sentences.en: And nobody sits at a parade wishing that everybody would stand still.
sentences.zh: 没有人会坐在游行队伍里，希望所有人都站着不动。

sentences.en: If the language stayed the way it was, it would be like a pressed flower in a book.
sentences.zh: 如果语言保持原样，它就像书里压扁的花朵。

sentences.en: Or as I say, I think it would be like some inflatable doll rather than a person.
sentences.zh: 或者正如我所说，我觉得它更像是一个充气娃娃，而不是一个人。

sentences.en: I think that it's better to think of language as a parade that either you're watching or,
sentences.zh: 我认为最好把语言看作一场游行，要么你在观看，要么，

sentences.en: frankly, that you're in, especially because the people are never going to stand still.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，你就在其中，尤其是因为人们永远不会静止不动。

sentences.en: It's never happened.
sentences.zh: 这种情况从未发生过。

sentences.en: It's never going to.
sentences.zh: 将来也不会发生。

sentences.en: And if you can enjoy it as a parade, instead of wondering why people keep walking,
sentences.zh: 如果你能把它当作一场游行来享受，而不是纳闷为什么人们一直在走，

sentences.en: instead of just sitting on chairs and blowing on their tubas and not moving,
sentences.zh: 而不是坐在椅子上吹着大号一动不动，

sentences.en: then you have more fun.
sentences.zh: 那你就会获得更多乐趣。

sentences.en: I want everybody to have the fun I'm having.
sentences.zh: 我希望每个人都能享受到我所拥有的这种乐趣。
